meta_description_ru: Читательские письма в журнал Outlet #057: вопросы о шрифтах Epson MX80/FT, подключении ZX Spectrum +3 к PC 486, ревизиях моделей +3 и советы Brian Gaff.
body_en_plain:
E V E N   M O R E   M A I L !


     May, 1992       Page  Reply

 George Caldwell......02    05
 Phil Parnell.........08    12
 Bill Coats...........13    15
 Carlo Malantrucco....16    18
 Chris Clayton........20    24
 Mike Pike............25    34
 Bob Hughes...........36    38

From: G. Caldwell, LONDONDERRY

Dear Ron,

Some time ago I wrote to you
asking you for information about
my Plus 3 computer and 3 1/2"
disk drive. The information I
received about these from OUTLET
was very useful. As a result of
your information I was able to
use the underline facility of my
MX80/FT Epsom printer and format
my 3 1/2" disks to 706K. I was
also able to transfer data and
backup games to 3 1/2" disk from
Multiface 3. 3" saved material.

I would now like to ask further
information about my Epson
printer; perhaps you could help.

Could you please tell me the
control codes to commence and
stop the following fonts on the
Epson MX80/FT printer: italics,
elite and proport. As with
underline these do not appear in
the manual I have. I would be
very grateful for your help in
this matter.

I've recently become a student
at the Open University and have
acquired my own P.C. (a very
powerful one - a 486/DX 25 MH
machine).Are there any interest-
ing things that can be achieved
between the two computers eg.
transferring screens, programs,
printouts etc? Although I have
this machine I would never give
up my Spectrum +3 because of the
great enjoyment I get from it.

By the way, I'm a grandfather
and thoroughly enjoy OUTLET on
Plus 3 disk.

Hope to hear from you soon.

        Yours faithfully,

         George Caldwell

Brian Gaff to George Caldwell


I am glad to hear you have had
success with the disc drive.
706K is certainly very useful to
have! On the printer side, I
find it odd that the manual does
not detail how to control such
basic features as font changes!

Obviously, without your actual
model of printer sitting here, I
cannot be sure this information
is correct, but here goes
anyway..

Italics:

ON  = CHR$ 27 + "4"
OFF = CHR$ 27 + "5"

Elite:
ON  = CHR$ 27 + "M"
OFF = CHR$ 27 + "P"

Proportional:
      CHR$ 27 + "p"
This is a toggle.Note:lower case
"p". I cannot test this last one
as my printer cannot support it.

Well,that PC sounds rather nice!
There are several Spectrum
emulators that should run almost
usably fast on such a machine.
There is also a nice utility
called 22NICE/22DISK that can
run CP/M2.2 on the PC and read
your 706K floppies. Both of the
above are Shareware.(BG Services
can supply them on 5.25"floppy
for `1- registration is then up
to you)

There is a PD program called
ZX2 that basically streams data
to the hard drive from the com2
port. It can be used as a
printer buffer for the +3. You
could do a COPY at 9600 baud,
and store the code on the PC
then print it as required. You
could do the same for text.

Specterm 2 can transfer via
Xmodem to a PC at around 4800
baud so this could be used to
store code on the PC. PCs can be
fun but the lack of technical
info and the unfriendliness of
DOS can make you crave for your
Speccy.
                           B.G.

From: Phil Parnell, LANCS.

Does anyone out there know how
to tell the different versions
of the +3 apart? I am assured
that there are different
versions of the same model like
the 48K Spectrum.

Now for a few messages. If you
are reading this, Gordon, thanks
for the Outdex mod you have
done. It is much easier to read
in this configuration.

Robert, did you send off that
form to the post office as it is
much quicker if you have. They
have probably been in touch by
now but if they haven't been
then they will be.

To end my letter I would like to
complain via outlet about the
poor service from PROPAC P.D.
Has anyone else had a similar
experience to me? I wrote off to
them and ordered 16 titles and
enclosed an s.a.e. Three months
later I had heard nothing,
although they were rather sharp
to cash my cheque.

So, on the offchance that my
return order had been lost I
wrote an enquiry, again with an
s.a.e enclosed. Another 3 or 4
weeks went by. Zip. I rang the
number in the advert in Outboard
and left a message. Nothing. In
a last ditch effort I wrote a
rather angry letter. A week
later a letter arrived!!

Success? No chance. "We will get
round to you eventually" was the
jist of the text. Get round to
me eventually! It's now been
about 5 months and it has cost
me almost as much in stationery,
stamps and telephone charges as
the cost of the P.D.

Eventually I got the disk and
they had put four extra utilit-
ies on by way of an apology. At
least that's something, I
thought. On loading up the disk
I found that about about half of
them were not what I had
ordered. The majority of what I
didn't order was OUTLET free-
ware! To be fair they were not
to know I subscribed to OUTLET
but it was the final straw (or
so I thought)...

NONE of the utilities on the
disk ran when selected from the
menu. ALL stopped with error
reports. There was even one with
a copyright message in the
listing!

Needless to say, I will not be
re-ordering from them and just
thought you should know as their
advert is in OUTBOARD. No one
can say I didn't give them a
chance. Three s.a.e's, a phone
call and 5 months wait is not
exactly what I call customer-
friendly!! Consider youselves
warned if you reply to their ad.

         Phil Parnell

Brian Cavers to Phil Parnell

Orders may get lost in the post
but three letters, a phone call
and five months' wait would try
anyone's patience. However, the
fact they put the extra programs
on your disc tells us they did
have some concern. I believe the
error reports are because they
are saved as "non-auto run" and
you need to enter RUN manually.

A copyright message does not
necessarily mean the program is
not in the public domain but it
would be nice if more programm-
ers would put a clear label like
our "FREEWARE" sticker!

                         - Brian

From: Bill Coats, STRATHCLYDE

Dear Brian/Ron,

Thanks for your suggestion
(Outletters, Disc 55) to get my
printer to operate without
having to BREAK and RUN.

After inserting the +3 BUG FIX
routine in FONTWIST.3 it worked
fine. I've also put it into
TASWORD II, WordMaster, and a +3
disc header reader program (PCW
magazine, Vol.7, No.17). The
disc reader has about 90 bytes
of machine code which have to be
poked, so, using CODELINE and
RELINO from Disc 49 (two really
useful utilities), I put the
bytes into a REM line and
renumbered it.

This means the program can be
used right away (no more waiting
for the m/code to be poked).

About TASWORD II (with TAS_EXTN
from Disc 24): if I print a
textfile, it can't be printed
again until the printer is
switched off and on again - a
case of the printer 'hanging-up'
instead of the computer.

Anyway, Brian, thanks again.

           Bill Coats

Brian Cavers to Bill Coats

The printer "hang up" is a bit
strange. Are you saying that
after printing a document then
Tasword 2 returns to the text
editor (or menu - I forget which
the original does) and you have
control but when you select to
print the document again the
printer does not respond?

Are you sure it's simply not off
line? Can you do a line feed by
going off line and pressing the
button on your printer?

                      Brian

This letter was sent directly to
Brian Gaff via the BB network
known as Fidonet. I thought it
might be of interest to others..

   From: Carlo Malantrucco
Msg Num: 2775 of 2786
     To: Brian Gaff
   Date: 03-25-92 17:41
   Subj: Outlet's Add-Enders
   Attr: Rec'd
   Conf: Spectrum [Echo]

I wrote to Ron & Brian Cavers to
ask for a Discovery version of
Outlet's Add-Enders: they told
me that I could subscribe to the
Outlet tape version, transfer
Add-Enders from tape to disk and
share it with other users
receiving the Outlet Discovery
version.

Well, recently I received from
Kees Versluis an utility to read
Disciple disks with the
Discovery drive so now I'm able
to transfer files from Disciple
to Discovery disks. Do you think
that I could subscribe to the
Disciple version of Outlet,
transfer Add-Enders to Discovery
disk and load it without any
problem?

Thank you. Carlo


Comments on Carlo Maluntrucco's
message from Brian Gaff...



The files will in most cases be
the same. The only difference
will be that the Disciple
version will use LOAD D1, and
not Microdrive syntax. [No need
to change because Disciple does
accept microdrive syntax - BC]
However, if you had used the
tape version, you would still
have had to alter the loaders.


Opus users must bear in mind
that to do as Carlo suggests,
you must have a double-sided 80
TR drive fitted to your Opus.

Brian Cavers suggests that you
purchase just one issue of the
Disciple version of Outlet at
the `2:50 price and see how it
converts. Is this program
Freeware?
                          B.G.

From: Chris Clayton,  CARLISLE

Dear Brian,

I hope you will publish this
letter as soon as possible for
reasons which should be clear.

I was very concerned to read the
letter from Keith Pirie of
Teachers Pet Software (in Issue
56) suggesting I had submitted a
SCREEN$ from their Clip Art
range as if it was my own work.

I appreciated your response
which sought to 'clear my name'
but it appeared that (not
surprisingly) you had forgotten
exactly how the SCREEN$ came to
be sent to you.

Quite a long time ago I sent in,
and you published, a review
article on Clip Art. In it I
described Teachers Pet Clip Art,
along with others and in
particular Daniel Garner, and
gave details of the cost and
their addresses.

I included on the cartridge one
or two SCREEN$ examples. Before
sending you the article I wrote
to Daniel Garner and Teachers
Pet explaining my intentions.
The former replied expressing
approval. I cannot recall if I
got a reply from Teachers Pet,
and if I didn't then, perhaps,
it would have been better for me
to have erased their examples
from the cartridge.

But as can be seen, there was no
intention whatever to
misrepresent. I was surprised to
see the SCREEN$ appearing, with
my name associated with it, more
than a year later.

Unfortunately, I no longer have
the article I wrote, but
presumably you can find it in
your OUTDEX (which I do not
maintain) --- in which case I
would very much appreciate your
sending it to Keith Pirie to
confirm my explanation.

I do feel that Keith should not
have sent the letter with its
unpleasant suggestions of
dishonesty nor should you have
published it, without contacting
me first.

In the light of recent cases, I
am wondering if I might be able
to take early retirement on the
damages I would get if it came
to court? (only joking!)

I am sending a copy of this
letter to Teachers Pet Software
requesting an apology.

             Yours,

        Chris Clayton

Brian Cavers to Chris Clayton

My apologies Chris. Your review
was in Issue 41 (January, 1991).
I was unable to find your letter
sending the review but I accept
what you say. It is just one of
those unfortunate misunderstand-
ings or perhaps,a record-keeping
error on my part. I should have
contacted you before publication
but it seemed a simple case of
innocently sending what seemed
to be public domain.

On Keith Pirie's part, I doubt
that he realized I would publish
his letter which I did simply to
remind others to be careful what
they contribute. I'll write to
Keith to explain.
                      - Brian

From: Mike Pike, NORTHALLERTON

Whilst reading last month's
OUTLET (issue 56), I came across
a few letters on which I would
like to comment (and hopefully
provide some help in the
process).

Firstly, John Webster asked for
details of converting graphics
files from the PC to SAM. I
thought it worth mentioning that
although the file format could
be found and the file translated
there is an additional factor
involved. Many graphics files on
the PC are in a compressed
format, mainly to save disk
space (an A4 size colour image
can occupy several megabytes!).

The problem is that there are
different types of compression.
For instance, take a TIF format
file. There are several types-
Uncompressed, Packbits, CCITT
and LZW to name a few. Each uses
its own method of compression,
and all look the same until you
analyse the file. Of course, you
need a different program to de-
compress each one.

Probably the easiest thing to do
is to make sure that the files
are of the uncompressed type.
This rules out the GIF format by
the way, which as far as I know
only exists in compressed
format. I hope this info will
help avoid a major headache for
someone!

Onto the next problem -R.Webster
with his Everyday Electronics
printer interface and PCB
Designer software. I myself
built this interface from the
article in the Jan '89 issue of
EE, so know how it works. It
uses a small program residing in
the printer buffer which is run
each time the machine is
switched on, and redirects
LPRINT and LLIST commands to the
printer interface.

The suggestion I make is
probably the obvious one - don't
try to use this interface and
the +D together, since the soft-
ware program will intercept all
LPRINT and LLIST commands before
they get to the +D.

Running the interface without
loading the software should work
OK though. The software does all
the work; the interface just
contains a Z80PIO chip.

Malcolm Perry brought up the
subject of sector numbering on
floppy disks, and how altering
the sequence in which they were
accessed could improve disk per-
formance.

Interestingly enough, the PC has
an unusual capability which
takes account of this. As many
people know, hard disks are used
to store large amounts of data
so that they can be accessed
quickly. Since large data files
are sometimes used, disk access
time becomes important.

The PC will only read the
sectors on a disk in the normal
sequence (0,1,2,etc.)  but when
formatting the hard disk, you
can actually change the order of
the sectors! This means they
don't have to be consecutively
numbered on the disk.

It also means that ALL software
will access the disk faster, not
just that specifically designed
to do so. This feature is known
as interleaving, and depends on
the machine's and the disk's
speed. Basically, what happens
is, the machine reads a sector
(e.g., sector 0) from the disk.
The disk,however, keeps spinning
so by the time the machine has
processed the information and

come back for sector 1, the
heads in the disk drive are
positioned over another sector
(such as sector 5). The machine
now has to wait for the disk to
spin round to sector 1 again.
(the same thing happens with
floppies, by the way).


However, by renaming what would
be sector 5 as sector 1, then no
wait is needed - the data is
ready to be retrieved.


A more complicated approach is
to change the order in which you
read the sectors - although you
can sometimes end up with a load
of jumbled-up data!

Don't forget, the order of the
sectors depends on the speed at
which the disk rotates, and the
speed of the CPU. The software
would have to be modified for
each machine and drive type.
Therefore, changing the disk
format is easier than changing
the software.

I don't know if it is possible
to change the format of a +D
disk to take account of this, so
maybe things will have to be
left as they are.

Finally, a whinge about a
software hire company. Spectrum
Software Hire of 32 Dursley Rd.,
Trowbridge, Wilts were mentioned
some time ago in OUTLETTERS.

I sent for their catalogue which
quickly arrived, and I ordered
what I thought would be a useful
title: "3D Electronic Workshop".
The title sounded interesting as
electronics is one of my other
hobbies. When the cassette
arrived at the end of December
it was entitled "3D Electronic
Worksheet" (not workshop). It
didn't sound what I wanted. On
running the program, it produced
3D bar graphs on the screen
(nothing to do with an electron-
ic workshop). I disgustedly sent
the tape back the same day,
asking(nicely) for a replacement
title, and explaining the prob-
lem. It was their mistake that
there was seemingly a printing
error in their catalogue.

Needless to say, I got no reply.
I wrote again, this time asking
for SSH to just credit me with
the amount.I got a response this
time - they cashed my cheque!
Sensing I was being ignored, I
wrote again demanding a full
refund within 14 days. That was
over three months ago and,you've
guessed it, not a word from SSH
since the original order.

I would have thought a small
enterprise (as SSH presumably
is) needs all the customers it
can get and can well do without
some bad publicity. However, in
my view they have had ample
opportunity to make amends (or
at least send a reply), so I
have had no option but to write
this letter..

Brian Cavers to Mike Pike

Thanks for the PC file info,Mike

Regarding the software for the
PCB DESIGNER, I understand it is
in machine code and specifically
set up for each interface and so
cannot be easily converted. Ron
Webster wants to use the soft-
ware provided (set up for the EE
interface) with the Disciple or
+D and it won't work.

Regarding, disc sector order, it
is worth reading Malcolm Perry's
recent OUTLETTER (OUTLET 56 I
think) about QUIKCOP which
prompted me to change the order
of sectors that it uses result-
ing in QUIKCOP 2 in OUTLET 56.

Mail-order businesses suffer a
lot from Post Office delivery
failures but many don't seem to
follow up complaints with the
same concern that we do. We give
a high priority to any complaint
about orders which is why we
offer money back on anything
without any question as to who's
right or wrong. We also accept
responsibility for delivery so
will despatch fresh goods if
lost in the post and then recoup
the loss from the Post Office.

It seems many small businesses
are not aware one can claim from
the Post Office even on normal,
(non-registered) delivery, at
least for small amounts.

                         - Brian

From: Bob Hughes, TRURO

Re:your reply to the letter from
Simon Strange in Issue 55 March,
regarding double line-feeds.

For some unknown reason (at
least to me) the Plus 3 sends a
signal via Ground Pin 14 to the
Printer. This seems to over-ride
the Dip switch setting to the
line-feed and creates a double
line if your program already
contains a line feed.

However, if Pin 14 is isolated
by using a bit of sticky tape,
the Dip switch can be then be
used to turn ON or OFF the line
feed. The +3 printer socket
diagram is shown on page 312 of
the +3 manual.

This works on a Citizen 120D
printer with a +3 but I have not
been able to check with any
other printers.

Hope this will be of interest.

           Bob Hughes

Brian Cavers to Bob Hughes

Thanks Bob. It's definitely of
interest but puzzles me further.
It seems one should NEVER send a
line-feed on the +3! This makes
it totally incompatible with any
software that already does. I
give up. I should have taken up
something simple like brain
surgery or quantum mechanics.

                        - Brian.

From: Mike Pike, NORTHALLERTON

Whilst reading last month's OUTLET (issue 56), I came across a few letters on which I would like to comment (and hopefully provide some help in the process).

Firstly, John Webster asked for details of converting graphics files from the PC to SAM. I thought it worth mentioning that although the file format could be found and the file translated there is an additional factor involved. Many graphics files on the PC are in a compressed format, mainly to save disk space (an A4 size colour image can occupy several megabytes!).

The problem is that there are different types of compression. For instance, take a TIF format file. There are several types- Uncompressed, Packbits, CCITT and LZW to name a few. Each uses its own method of compression, and all look the same until you analyse the file. Of course, you need a different program to de- compress each one.

Probably the easiest thing to do is to make sure that the files are of the uncompressed type. This rules out the GIF format by the way, which as far as I know only exists in compressed format. I hope this info will help avoid a major headache for someone!

Onto the next problem -R.Webster with his Everyday Electronics printer interface and PCB Designer software. I myself built this interface from the article in the Jan '89 issue of EE, so know how it works. It uses a small program residing in the printer buffer which is run each time the machine is switched on, and redirects LPRINT and LLIST commands to the printer interface.

The suggestion I make is probably the obvious one - don't try to use this interface and the +D together, since the soft- ware program will intercept all LPRINT and LLIST commands before they get to the +D.

Running the interface without loading the software should work OK though. The software does all the work; the interface just contains a Z80PIO chip.

Malcolm Perry brought up the subject of sector numbering on floppy disks, and how altering the sequence in which they were accessed could improve disk per- formance.

Interestingly enough, the PC has an unusual capability which takes account of this. As many people know, hard disks are used to store large amounts of data so that they can be accessed quickly. Since large data files are sometimes used, disk access time becomes important.

The PC will only read the sectors on a disk in the normal sequence (0,1,2,etc.)  but when formatting the hard disk, you can actually change the order of the sectors! This means they don't have to be consecutively numbered on the disk.

It also means that ALL software will access the disk faster, not just that specifically designed to do so. This feature is known as interleaving, and depends on the machine's and the disk's speed. Basically, what happens is, the machine reads a sector (e.g., sector 0) from the disk. The disk,however, keeps spinning so by the time the machine has processed the information and

come back for sector 1, the heads in the disk drive are positioned over another sector (such as sector 5). The machine now has to wait for the disk to spin round to sector 1 again. (the same thing happens with floppies, by the way).

However, by renaming what would be sector 5 as sector 1, then no wait is needed - the data is ready to be retrieved.

A more complicated approach is to change the order in which you read the sectors - although you can sometimes end up with a load of jumbled-up data!

Don't forget, the order of the sectors depends on the speed at which the disk rotates, and the speed of the CPU. The software would have to be modified for each machine and drive type. Therefore, changing the disk format is easier than changing the software.

I don't know if it is possible to change the format of a +D disk to take account of this, so maybe things will have to be left as they are.

Finally, a whinge about a software hire company. Spectrum Software Hire of 32 Dursley Rd., Trowbridge, Wilts were mentioned some time ago in OUTLETTERS.

I sent for their catalogue which quickly arrived, and I ordered what I thought would be a useful title: "3D Electronic Workshop". The title sounded interesting as electronics is one of my other hobbies. When the cassette arrived at the end of December it was entitled "3D Electronic Worksheet" (not workshop). It didn't sound what I wanted. On running the program, it produced 3D bar graphs on the screen (nothing to do with an electron- ic workshop). I disgustedly sent the tape back the same day, asking(nicely) for a replacement title, and explaining the prob- lem. It was their mistake that there was seemingly a printing error in their catalogue.

Needless to say, I got no reply. I wrote again, this time asking for SSH to just credit me with the amount.I got a response this time - they cashed my cheque! Sensing I was being ignored, I wrote again demanding a full refund within 14 days. That was over three months ago and,you've guessed it, not a word from SSH since the original order.

I would have thought a small enterprise (as SSH presumably is) needs all the customers it can get and can well do without some bad publicity. However, in my view they have had ample opportunity to make amends (or at least send a reply), so I have had no option but to write this letter..

Brian Cavers to Mike Pike

From: Bob Hughes, TRURO

Re:your reply to the letter from Simon Strange in Issue 55 March, regarding double line-feeds.

For some unknown reason (at least to me) the Plus 3 sends a signal via Ground Pin 14 to the Printer. This seems to over-ride the Dip switch setting to the line-feed and creates a double line if your program already contains a line feed.

However, if Pin 14 is isolated by using a bit of sticky tape, the Dip switch can be then be used to turn ON or OFF the line feed. The +3 printer socket diagram is shown on page 312 of the +3 manual.

This works on a Citizen 120D printer with a +3 but I have not been able to check with any other printers.

Hope this will be of interest.

Bob Hughes

Thanks Bob. It's definitely of interest but puzzles me further. It seems one should NEVER send a line-feed on the +3! This makes it totally incompatible with any software that already does. I give up. I should have taken up something simple like brain surgery or quantum mechanics.

### От: Mike Pike, NORTHALLERTON

Читая прошлый номер OUTLET (выпуск 56), я наткнулся на несколько писем, которые мне хотелось бы прокомментировать (и, надеюсь, попутно чем-то помочь).

Во-первых, John Webster спрашивал о деталях конвертации графических файлов с PC на SAM. Мне показалось важным отметить: хотя формат файла можно выяснить и перевести данные, здесь есть дополнительный фактор. Многие графические файлы на PC хранятся в сжатом виде, главным образом для экономии места на диске (цветное изображение формата A4 может занимать несколько мегабайт!).

Проблема в том, что существуют разные типы сжатия. Взять, к примеру, формат TIF. У него есть несколько разновидностей — Uncompressed, Packbits, CCITT и LZW, и это лишь малая часть. Каждая использует свой собственный метод сжатия, и все они выглядят одинаково, пока не проанализируешь сам файл. Разумеется, для распаковки каждого из них нужна отдельная программа.

Пожалуй, проще всего убедиться, что файлы сохранены без сжатия (uncompressed). Это, кстати, сразу исключает формат GIF, который, насколько мне известно, существует только в сжатом виде. Надеюсь, эта информация избавит кого-то от сильной головной боли!

Перейдем к следующей проблеме — R. Webster с его интерфейсом принтера из Everyday Electronics и программой PCB Designer. Я сам собирал этот интерфейс по статье из январского номера EE за 1989 год, так что знаю, как он работает. Он использует небольшую программку, находящуюся в буфере принтера, которая запускается при каждом включении компьютера и перенаправляет команды LPRINT и LLIST на интерфейс принтера.

Мой совет, вероятно, очевиден: не пытайтесь использовать этот интерфейс одновременно с +D, поскольку программа будет перехватывать все команды LPRINT и LLIST до того, как они дойдут до +D.

Впрочем, запуск интерфейса без загрузки этой программы должен работать нормально. Всю работу выполняет софт; сам интерфейс содержит лишь микросхему Z80PIO.

Malcolm Perry поднял тему нумерации секторов на гибких дисках и того, как изменение порядка обращения к ним может повысить производительность дисковода.

Любопытно, что у PC есть необычная возможность, учитывающая этот момент. Как многие знают, жесткие диски используются для хранения больших объемов данных с целью быстрого доступа к ним. Поскольку файлы иногда бывают очень большими, время доступа к диску становится критичным.

PC считывает секторы на диске только в стандартной последовательности (0, 1, 2 и т. д.), но при форматировании жесткого диска вы можете изменить физический порядок секторов! Это означает, что им вовсе не обязательно идти на диске строго по порядку номеров.

Это также означает, что ВСЕ программы станут обращаться к диску быстрее, а не только те, что были специально для этого написаны. Эта особенность называется чередованием секторов (interleaving) и зависит от скорости работы машины и накопителя. Грубо говоря, происходит следующее: компьютер считывает с диска сектор (например, сектор 0). Диск тем временем продолжает вращаться, и к моменту, когда компьютер обработал информацию и готов прочесть сектор 1, головки дисковода уже находятся над другим сектором (скажем, над сектором 5). Теперь компьютеру приходится ждать, пока диск сделает полный оборот и снова подставит сектор 1. (С дискетами, кстати, происходит ровно то же самое).

Однако если переименовать то, что должно было быть сектором 5, в сектор 1, ждать не придется — данные сразу готовы к считыванию.

Более сложный подход — менять порядок, в котором секторы считываются программно, хотя в этом случае можно получить кучу перемешанных данных!

Не забывайте: порядок секторов зависит от скорости вращения диска и тактовой частоты процессора. Программу пришлось бы модифицировать под каждую конкретную машину и тип дисковода. Поэтому изменить формат диска намного проще, чем переделывать софт.

Не знаю, возможно ли изменить формат диска +D с учетом этого нюанса, так что, возможно, всё придется оставить как есть.

И напоследок — жалоба на компанию по прокату программного обеспечения. Spectrum Software Hire (SSH) из 32 Dursley Rd., Trowbridge, Wilts упоминалась некоторое время назад в OUTLETTERS.
